plan.title: ci: nightly coverage and Windows full-suite runs that release readiness reuses

narratives.Description: Once a release reuses CI (#6791, S1 of #6845), coverage against the floor and the full Windows suite run nowhere before a release ships. This story adds one scheduled workflow with a Linux coverage lane and a Windows full-suite lane on the same master commit, a reporting job that keeps one durable tracking issue per lane, and a nightly conjunct on the merged Step 5 CI reuse rule that release:run readiness prints and Step 5 re-evaluates. Nothing changes on the PR or merge-queue path and no required check is added.
narratives.Overview:
1. Workflow. `.github/workflows/nightly.yml` runs on `schedule` (one cron a day) and `workflow_dispatch`, and on no other event. Every job runs only when the ref is `refs/heads/master`, and each lane checks out `github.sha`, so both lanes of one run test the same commit. `concurrency: nightly` without cancel. Workflow permissions are `contents: read`; only the reporting job gets `issues: write`. Job names do not equal a required check name.
2. Preparation. Both lanes use the `merge-gate-primary` preparation: Node from `.nvmrc`, corepack pnpm, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, Task, Go, uv and the tip dogfood materialize (which builds the checkout). Windows uses the Windows equivalents of the same steps. Before the tests, each lane fails as a setup failure unless `task --version` succeeds and `packages/cli/dist/bin.js` exists.
3. Coverage lane, `Nightly coverage (Linux)`, on `ubuntu-latest` with `timeout-minutes: 60`: `pnpm run test` (vitest with `--coverage` and the `vitest.config.ts` floor). No `task check:merge` and no coverage-debt flag. It uploads `coverage/coverage-final.json` when it exists.
4. Windows lane, `Nightly full suite (Windows)`, on `windows-latest` with `timeout-minutes: 240`: `pnpm exec vitest run` without coverage, both vitest projects. The coverage floor is read on Linux only.
5. Reporting. A job `if: always()` after both lanes classifies each lane as `passed`, `test-failure`, `setup-failure`, `timed-out-or-cancelled` or `report-unavailable`, from the job and step results. For each lane there is one durable tracking issue, found by its hidden body marker among issues opened by `github-actions[bot]`, open or closed. On a red lane it reopens the issue (or creates it once) and comments with the lane, the outcome class, the SHA, the run id and attempt, the run URL, and the failing test files and the four coverage totals when a report exists; an absent value is written as unknown, never as zero. On a passed lane it comments and closes an open issue. A comment for the same run id and attempt is not posted twice. The issue is assigned to the login in the repository variable `NIGHTLY_OWNER`; when it is unset the run summary says no one was assigned. Neither title nor body contains `coverage-debt`. Test output is written to a file and passed with `--body-file`, never into a shell command. A failure of the reporting job fails the run.
6. Release reuse. Readiness and Step 5 read the nightly workflow runs. For each lane, the witness is the newest run whose head commit tree equals the clean Step 5 input tree; the lane is reusable only when the latest attempt of that lane in that run concluded `success`. A pending, failed or missing latest attempt is not reusable, and an older success is never used. The #6845 Step 5 reuse also requires both lanes reusable. Readiness prints per lane the status, run URL and head SHA. When a lane is not reusable, readiness says before the mint which lane and why, that the full local Step 5 check will run and about how long, and prints the command to start the workflow on master. Step 5 evaluates the rule again and continues without a prompt either way.
7. Host boundary. When the local Step 5 fallback runs on a host that is not Windows and the Windows lane is not reusable, readiness and Step 5 print that the Windows suite did not run for this release. No refusal is added.
8. Docs. The release skill and `docs/RELEASING.md` say where coverage and the Windows suite run, the reuse rule, the fallback, the Windows host boundary and how a red lane is reported.
9. Build order. One PR, built after #6845 merges.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the workflow file, then its only triggers are `schedule` and `workflow_dispatch`, no job name equals `TypeScript (build + lint)` or `Merge gate (task check)`, and only the reporting job has `issues: write`.
- Given a dispatch on a ref other than master, then no lane runs.
- Given a lane where Task is missing or `packages/cli/dist/bin.js` is absent, then the lane fails as a setup failure before the tests run.
- Given a red lane with no tracking issue, then one issue is created; given a closed tracking issue and a new red run, then that issue is reopened and no second issue is created.
- Given the reporting job runs twice for the same run id and attempt, then only one comment is posted.
- Given a lane that timed out or failed in setup, then the comment names that outcome class and writes missing totals as unknown.
- Given a passed lane and an open tracking issue, then the issue gets a comment and is closed.
- Given a nightly run whose head tree equals the clean Step 5 input tree and whose latest attempt of both lanes succeeded, when the #6845 reuse rule also holds, then Step 5 skips the local check and prints both run URLs.
- Given a green nightly run on an ancestor whose tree differs from the Step 5 input tree, then Step 5 does not reuse it and runs the full local check.
- Given a matching run whose latest attempt of a lane failed or is pending, also when an earlier attempt succeeded, then that lane is not reusable.
- Given a lane is not reusable at readiness, then readiness says before the mint which lane and why, that the full local check will run, and prints the dispatch command.
- Given the fallback runs on a non-Windows host and the Windows lane is not reusable, then readiness and Step 5 print that the Windows suite did not run.
- Given the docs, then the release skill and `docs/RELEASING.md` name where coverage and the Windows suite run and the reuse rule.
narratives.Constraint:
- Reusing a nightly result from an ancestor or a different tree, with or without an age limit or a printed commit count (comment 7044533420 finding 1).
- Setting up the Windows lane like the narrow Windows dispatch job, so tests that need Task or the built CLI return early (comment 7044533420 finding 2).
- Reporting only failing tests, or writing a missing total as zero (comment 7044533420 finding 3).
- A new issue for each failure, an unassigned issue with no owner named, or coverage-debt markers on the nightly issue (comment 7044533420 finding 4).
- Claiming the local fallback tests Windows on a non-Windows host (comment 7044533420 finding 5).
- Running `task check:merge` in the nightly, any job on `pull_request` or `merge_group`, a new required check, automatic test retries, or a slow-test lane.
- Skipping a nightly run on an unchanged tree in this version.
narratives.ImplementationPlan: Build on the merged #6845 release:run surfaces, not planned ones. The #6791 reuse rule shipped in S1 (#6898): packages/core/src/release/ci-reuse.ts (evaluateCiReuse, decideCiReuseFromRuns, RELEASE_CI_REUSE_REQUIRED_CHECKS; its header already names #6849 as the coverage gap closer). Readiness shipped in S3 (#6876, PR #7010): packages/core/src/release/run-readiness.ts (ciReuseAtTip, readinessCiLines, runReleaseReadiness, formatReadiness). Step 5 re-evaluation is evaluateStep5CiReuse in packages/core/src/release/pipeline.ts. S4 (#6877) and S5 (#6878) are merged; S5 rewrote the release skill runbook and docs/RELEASING.md, so the docs edit extends that runbook. Add the nightly lane conjunct in a new nightly-reuse.ts read by ci-reuse.ts, so readiness and Step 5 share one rule. Notes for the build: (1) Go is retired from master (#6863, after the arc): clause 2's 'same preparation as merge-gate-primary' means the current job steps, which have no Go step; do not add setup-go. (2) Collect failing test files with vitest CLI reporter flags (for example --reporter=json --outputFile) rather than editing vitest.config.ts, which is an evaluator surface (#3156) and would need xbrief/evaluator-surface-disposition.json. (3) No change to ci.yml, required checks, branch protection or rulesets. (4) The NIGHTLY_OWNER repository variable is an operator setting.
narratives.UserStory: As a release operator, I want a daily coverage run and a daily Windows full-suite run that release readiness reuses only on the same tree, so that a release that skips the local Step 5 check still ships code that was measured for coverage and tested on Windows.

## In plain English
Coverage is no longer measured on pull requests (#6041). Today it is measured only at release Step 5, which runs the whole suite with coverage on the operator's Windows machine and takes up to an hour. The merge gate runs the whole suite on Linux for every PR and queue run, without coverage, and CI runs only a short Windows dispatch check. #6845 (already arced) lets a release reuse the green CI result and skip Step 5 without asking. After that, nothing measures coverage and nothing runs the whole suite on Windows before a release ships.

The operator wants speed and still wants that testing. The recommended fix moves both runs off the PR path into one scheduled daily workflow on the master tip, reports a red run in one tracking issue per lane, and lets release readiness reuse a recent green run. When the run is missing, old or red, the release takes today's local Step 5 path instead. No PR or merge-queue job changes and no new PR gate is added.

## Operator decisions (Scott, recorded as constraints)
- In his words: "task check no longers runs anywhere else anymore? then perhaps we can have it run after a release or once a day. need ideas we want speed but still need testing". He then asked for options 1 to 3 from that discussion to go into this issue.
- He wants this in the next release: one PR if possible, split only if it cannot be one.
- Prefer designs that remove work from the PR path rather than add gates. A release-readiness check is preferred over a new PR gate.

## Pains
- P1 — Once a release reuses CI (#6845), coverage against the floor is measured nowhere before the release, so a coverage collapse can ship without anyone seeing it.
- P2 — Once a release reuses CI, the full test suite runs on Windows nowhere before the release, so a Windows-only failure can ship.

## Constraints (not pains)
- PR and merge-queue time must not change: no new job on `pull_request`, `push` or `merge_group`, and no new required check.
- No new prompt and no new refusal in the release run. When the scheduled result cannot be reused, the release is no worse than today: it runs the existing local Step 5.
- A red scheduled run must reach a person without opening a new issue every night.

## Out of scope (named, not pains)
- #6850, #6851, #6852, #6853, #6854, #6855, #6856: PR and merge-queue speed. This arc changes nothing on the PR path.
- #6862: the one slow test file in the merge gate. It is arced in parallel. This workflow runs whatever suite exists and adds no slow-test lane or marker (CONTRIBUTING.md § Slow tests still has none).
- #6845: the `release:run` verb and its CI reuse rule (bound lean item 3: reuse when the clean Step 5 input tree equals the fetched tip tree and the latest required check runs on that tip succeeded). This arc adds a conjunct to that reuse; it does not rebuild it. Its open item, "a reused cut runs no host coverage", is what this arc answers.
- Changing the coverage floor. The issue body says "85%"; the floor in `vitest.config.ts` is 75 on all four metrics. The scheduled run uses the config as it is.

## Anchors at the dispatch SHA
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` 3-10: triggers are `pull_request`, `push` to master and `merge_group`; no workflow in `.github/workflows/` has a `schedule` trigger. 56-81: the required checks are the two aggregators `TypeScript (build + lint)` and `Merge gate (task check)`; a master push can reuse a passed queue run (#6584, 195-216). 228-277: `merge-gate-primary` installs pnpm, Task, Go and uv, materializes the tip dogfood runtime and runs `task check:merge`. 595-604: the Windows job is a task-dispatch regression, not the suite.
- `Taskfile.yml` 427-431 and 433-511: `check:merge` is `check:framework-source`: `ts:check-lane` plus about 60 `verify:*` gates.
- `packages/core/src/ts-check-lane/run-lane.ts` 44-58: the lane runs vitest with `--coverage` only under `DEFT_RELEASE_PREFLIGHT=1` (release Step 5); CI and ordinary runs use `pnpm exec vitest run`.
- `package.json` 15: `test` is `vitest run --coverage`. `vitest.config.ts` 24-26 and 75-80: coverage floor 75 on lines, functions, branches and statements, the same on win32 and Linux; 287-310: `unit` and `spawn-heavy` projects; win32 timeouts are 240s.
- `packages/core/src/vitest-runner/coverage-debt.ts` 5-10: `COVERAGE_GOAL` is 85 (the debt-hatch goal, not the floor).
- `packages/core/src/release/coverage-debt-ledger.ts` 130-170: release Step 5 treats any open issue matching the searches `coverage-debt in:title,body` or `allow-coverage-debt in:body` as open debt, which blocks a second soft-pass.
- `packages/core/src/release/pipeline.ts` 328-440: Step 5 (skip-ci incident path, suite stamp, host coverage run).
- `docs/RELEASING.md` 94-104: #6041 decision (merge path is coverage-free; release Step 5 is the host coverage run; Ubuntu is the accepted coverage floor reader for win32 residuals). 149-180: the coverage-debt hatch and ledger.
- `content/skills/deft-directive-release/SKILL.md` 92: readiness reads the two required checks on the tip.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` 200-213: no slow-test lane exists; flaky tests must be fixed, not hidden.
- The repository is public, so GitHub-hosted standard runners cost nothing; Blacksmith runners are paid.

## Recommended mechanism (the thing to critique)
- R1. One workflow, `.github/workflows/nightly.yml`, triggered only by `schedule` (one cron a day) and `workflow_dispatch` (no inputs, master only). `concurrency: nightly` with no cancel. metadata.issueBody:
Coverage measurement and the full Windows suite run only at release Step 5 (#6041 took coverage off the merge path). The merge gate runs the full test suite on Linux for every PR and queue run, but it runs no coverage, and CI has only a narrow Windows dispatch check. #6845 makes a release reuse CI on a matching tip and skip Step 5 without asking. After that, coverage and the full Windows suite would run nowhere. The repo has no scheduled workflows.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A scheduled workflow runs the suite with coverage and the 85% thresholds on the delivery-branch tip once a day. When it fails, it opens or updates one coverage-debt issue; it never opens a duplicate.
- [ ] A scheduled workflow runs the full suite on a Windows runner on the same tip once a day. When it fails, it opens or updates one tracking issue that names the failing tests.
- [ ] Release readiness (#6845) reads both results. If both are green on an ancestor of the release tree within 24 hours, readiness reuses them with no prompt. If either is stale or red, readiness warns before the mint and runs the missing one.
- [ ] Neither nightly job runs on pull requests or merge_group, so PR and queue time do not change.
- [ ] The release skill and docs/RELEASING.md say where coverage and Windows testing now run.

sentences: Workflow. `.github/workflows/nightly.yml` runs on `schedule` (one cron a day) and `workflow_dispatch`, and on no other event. Every job runs only when the ref is `refs/heads/master`, and each lane checks out `github.sha`, so both lanes of one run test the same commit. `concurrency: nightly` without cancel. Workflow permissions are `contents: read`; only the reporting job gets `issues: write`. Job names do not equal a required check name.

Preparation. Both lanes use the `merge-gate-primary` preparation: Node from `.nvmrc`, corepack pnpm, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, Task, Go, uv and the tip dogfood materialize (which builds the checkout). Windows uses the Windows equivalents of the same steps. Before the tests, each lane fails as a setup failure unless `task --version` succeeds and `packages/cli/dist/bin.js` exists.

Coverage lane, `Nightly coverage (Linux)`, on `ubuntu-latest` with `timeout-minutes: 60`: `pnpm run test` (vitest with `--coverage` and the `vitest.config.ts` floor). No `task check:merge` and no coverage-debt flag. It uploads `coverage/coverage-final.json` when it exists.
Windows lane, `Nightly full suite (Windows)`, on `windows-latest` with `timeout-minutes: 240`: `pnpm exec vitest run` without coverage, both vitest projects. The coverage floor is read on Linux only.

Reporting. A job `if: always()` after both lanes classifies each lane as `passed`, `test-failure`, `setup-failure`, `timed-out-or-cancelled` or `report-unavailable`, from the job and step results. For each lane there is one durable tracking issue, found by its hidden body marker among issues opened by `github-actions[bot]`, open or closed. On a red lane it reopens the issue (or creates it once) and comments with the lane, the outcome class, the SHA, the run id and attempt, the run URL, and the failing test files and the four coverage totals when a report exists; an absent value is written as unknown, never as zero. On a passed lane it comments and closes an open issue. A comment for the same run id and attempt is not posted twice. The issue is assigned to the login in the repository variable `NIGHTLY_OWNER`; when it is unset the run summary says no one was assigned. Neither title nor body contains `coverage-debt`. Test output is written to a file and passed with `--body-file`, never into a shell command. A failure of the reporting job fails the run.

Release reuse. Readiness and Step 5 read the nightly workflow runs. For each lane, the witness is the newest run whose head commit tree equals the clean Step 5 input tree; the lane is reusable only when the latest attempt of that lane in that run concluded `success`. A pending, failed or missing latest attempt is not reusable, and an older success is never used. The #6845 Step 5 reuse also requires both lanes reusable. Readiness prints per lane the status, run URL and head SHA. When a lane is not reusable, readiness says before the mint which lane and why, that the full local Step 5 check will run and about how long, and prints the command to start the workflow on master. Step 5 evaluates the rule again and continues without a prompt either way.

Host boundary. When the local Step 5 fallback runs on a host that is not Windows and the Windows lane is not reusable, readiness and Step 5 print that the Windows suite did not run for this release. No refusal is added.
